definitions.implementation_status: Offline implementation/workflow status only; implemented is not physically verified.
definitions.applicability: expected remains subject to control-level source audit; pending-audit must not be silently excluded.
definitions.completion: Every applicable feature needs source mapping, implementation, automated evidence and applicable hardware/service results.
definitions.percentage: No overall completion percentage is published while the denominator and applicability remain unresolved.

features.title: Wired USB discovery and connect
features.notes: Catalog USB VID/PID is 3151:5002. Bluetooth is 3151:5004; do not interchange them.

features.title: Bluetooth discovery and connect
features.notes: Bluetooth framing is implemented; sysfs detected Glyph at /dev/hidraw0 on 2026-09-09. root:root mode0600 prevents command verification by this user.

features.title: 2.4G receiver discovery and connect
features.notes: Vendor generic 24G status resolves a runtime keyboard ID through the shared model catalog and forwards commands through a paired dongle. No Glyph-specific receiver PID/pairing fixture has been established; receiver support and hardware verification remain pending.

features.title: Identity and firmware display
features.notes: Settings shows the connected model, internal ID, actual transport and raw USB firmware code captured at connection. Simulator UI checked; other component versions and physical identity remain unverified.

features.title: Battery and online state
features.notes: Rate-limited five-second Bluetooth status requests and bounded notification reads update raw battery and online state under the transport lock, with separate report ages. UI exposes only valid 0–100 battery reports and last online status; USB/absent reports are not synthesized. Request framing is traced to the macOS bridge; charging and physical telemetry remain unverified.

features.title: Disconnect, reconnect, and stale-state reset
features.notes: Idle UI polling refreshes device metadata and session state. A missing or changed command collection or DeviceUnavailable operation clears the session, pending vendor import, audio/live lighting and system refresh. New connections get a distinct session identity. Stale poll results cannot overwrite explicit connection actions; physical hotplug and transport switches remain unverified.

features.title: Sleep/wake or transport-change continuity
features.notes: Returned/new transport collections appear through metadata polling and can be explicitly connected. No writes or streams replay automatically. Sleep/wake telemetry, automatic resume and physical suspend behavior remain unfinished; a sleeping device retained in sysfs may still appear connected.

features.title: Read and edit normal keymap
features.notes: The graphical keyboard action editor exposes both key bytes and all eight modifier bits, with simulator readback and narrow-viewport checks. Other action types and vendor restrictions still require control-level reconciliation; hardware verification remains pending.

features.title: Knob/encoder actions
features.notes: Three source-mapped knob inputs are selectable on Main. Individual assignment rejects held macros and Fn edits; GUI disables those choices and blocks raw held actions. Both vendor bundles confirm shared predicates apply via Glyph knobKeyCodes. Both vendor bulk writers preserve supplied knob actions without individual editor exclusions; Linux import/restore preservation is covered by simulated round trips. The Glyph full Fn packet sequence now has vendor-derived offline fixtures; physical knob behavior and Fn persistence remain unverified.

features.title: Macro editor/import/export
features.notes: Semantic JSON editing/import/export and captured key/button pair insertion exist. Event capture preserves direction/timing and raw load snapshots; pair insertion validates capacity before changing the draft. Vendor configuration-file compatibility remains open.

features.title: Macro delays, repeats, and playback modes
features.notes: Repeat editing and separate Keymap count/toggle/held binding controls exist. Vendor metadata and eventual library-to-assignment workflow need end-to-end comparison; physical playback remains unverified.

features.title: Mouse-motion macro semantics
features.notes: Vendor position maps to signed dx/dy; UI bounds -127..127, Linux byte format -128..127. Shared encoder/decoder disagree on compact motion delay; Linux uses explicit long delays. Axis orientation, timing and -128 physical acceptance remain unverified.

features.title: Macro recording and playback verification
features.notes: Focused keyboard and mouse-button recording support measured/fixed timing and validated draft replacement. Reserved-key workflow comparison and physical playback verification remain open. Audited vendor recorder has no continuous-motion or wheel listener.

features.title: Named macro library and local persistence
features.notes: Persistent local named entries support create, rename, update, delete, explicit editor loading and playback preferences. Revision checks protect concurrent updates. Assignment remains a separate Keymap workflow; vendor service synchronization and hardware playback are unverified.

features.title: Edit per-key RGB picture pixels
features.notes: Visual painting covers 86 layout entries using the source-derived crosswalk; all 126 raw RGB slots remain editable. Draft undo/redo retains up to 100 edits. Five nonvisible nonzero matrix records remain unexplained; physical LED correspondence and the full vendor editing workflow audit remain open.

features.title: Picture import/export and full bank correspondence
features.notes: Independent 126-color JSON import/export and offline creation/fill exist, with destination preservation and full-array simulated round trips. Source-derived86-key mapping available; physical correspondence, vendor saved-record management/file compatibility remain open.

features.title: Host live-light USB gating
features.notes: Wired USB and firmware-flag-gated RGB frames plus explicit browser screen capture, per-session stale-request rejection and stop restoration. Audio now has explicit PipeWire output-monitor discovery/capture and an independent 32-band preview DSP with the seven vendor-bounded controls; it does not save PCM. Five rhythm modes, scale/colors and explicit optional audio-to-keyboard streaming now share the USB live-light session. Physical LED mapping, real capture/throughput and full vendor layout/audio/lifecycle parity remain unverified or incomplete.

features.title: Live-light capture/stream lifecycle
features.notes: Browser screen capture includes all eight vendor centered crop ratios, default/reset 2.35:1, source-resize recalculation, in-app selection retention and RGB preview. Session cleanup and stale-request rejection exist. Audio capture/preview has a five-second polling lease and cleanup, but uses synthetic/offline tests only; five rhythm renderers, scale/colors and optional keyboard streaming are integrated. Triple circle and Triangle retain an inactive rightmost shape because the native stream length/expansion remains unverified. Rhythm position/size/rotation controls, bounds and resets now transform a fixed 640x360 Linux workspace into21x6RGB; real canvas crop/rotation and browser lifecycle are tested offline. Physical LED mapping, real capture/throughput, native visual equivalence and host lifecycle remain incomplete or unverified. Vendor rhythm layout controls do not apply to screen mode.

features.title: Still-image conversion and screen upload
features.notes: Offline preparation validates all converted frames and previews their actual RGB565 pixels, with manual frame inspection, approximate desktop playback, frame count and effective timing. Zero-delay animations retain manual inspection only. Explicit upload reuses the prepared source. Full editor workflows, physical rendering and transport verification remain open. Rendered Windows/macOS upload controls require wired USB for both stills and animations; backend and UI now enforce the actual connected transport. Offline editing remains available on all transports.

features.title: Animation conversion, timing, and frame capacity
features.notes: Offline preparation validates all converted frames and previews their actual RGB565 pixels, with manual frame inspection, approximate desktop playback, frame count and effective timing. Zero-delay animations retain manual inspection only. Explicit upload reuses the prepared source. Full editor workflows, physical rendering and transport verification remain open. Glyph animation uploads require classified wired USB; the GUI uses connected transport metadata. Bluetooth/unknown transport cannot bypass the gate through multi-frame screen uploads. Rendered Windows/macOS upload controls require wired USB for both stills and animations; backend and UI now enforce the actual connected transport. Offline editing remains available on all transports.

features.title: Display bank selection, clear, and asset editor
features.notes: Five still destinations and a persistent named asset library support offline save/load/delete, original-source retention and portable JSON interchange. Frame insertion, copy-previous, deletion, clearing, painting, image placement and bounded undo/redo are implemented. Glyph screen erase now has an internal complete protocol transaction: one AC request, checked ACK and descriptor-scoped unsolicited completion reception while holding transport ownership. It never infers completion from the vendor55-second progress timer or retries erase automatically. The native adapter uses the same HID path for commands and incoming reports. The GUI now uses a journaled background erase with elapsed-time progress, global device-access exclusion and explicit uncertain-outcome acknowledgement followed by reconnect. It survives browser navigation/reload and never resumes an interrupted server operation. Physical bank behavior and hardware verification remain open.

features.title: Display transfer interruption and retry handling
features.notes: Prepare acceptance polling and bounded failure handling exist. Pixel readback has not been found; do not invent a pixel query. Recovery and actual display output still require verification. Internal erase waits have bounded completion deadlines, cancellation and stale-report draining; timeout or interruption does not resend AC or imply completed erasure. Application erase recovery now persists the operation before sending, retains blocked uncertainty on interruption or result-persistence failure and requires exact-operation acknowledgement plus reconnect. Physical interruption testing remains pending.

features.title: Background refresh, suspend, and lifecycle updates
features.notes: Explicit server-owned refresh survives app navigation and stops on disconnect, replacement, reset, restore, shutdown or sampling/transport error. No autostart or suspend/resume integration; vendor lifecycle comparison and physical display verification remain open. Both platform workers disable system-information synchronization during screen/music-follow lighting. Linux now stops refresh on live-session acquisition or main host-follow effect selection, rejects restarting it while either is active, and requires explicit restart afterward; onboard/side lighting remains independent.

features.title: Weather synchronization and unit selection
features.notes: The vendor weather control requires screen.canWeather and its unit selector requires canweatherUnit. Glyph model3059 has neither flag in both reference installers; the shared YC3123 weather method is a false-returning stub. This is an exclusion for the audited baseline, not a claim about future firmware.

features.title: Backup managed keyboard state
features.notes: Glyph snapshots capture all256macro slots, keymaps, custom RGB banks and exposed settings. Offline restore preview validates the entire snapshot and reports counts and omissions before writes; partial legacy macro snapshots preserve omitted slots and now report their count. Screen assets and vendor configuration-file restore remain incomplete; physical verification is open.

features.title: Preserve unreferenced macro slots
features.notes: Ordinary Glyph backups now capture all256slots, including raw/empty/unreferenced entries. Complete restores restore those entries; older partial snapshots preserve omitted slots. Hardware verification remains open.

features.title: Vendor local configurations and interchange
features.notes: Named Linux key-layer configurations support save, rename, delete, preview and verified apply. Entries retain Main/Fn OS identity and use optimistic revisions. Vendor database interchange, service sharing remains unfinished; Linux snapshots and this library are separate formats. Physical verification is pending. An offline vendor-record preview now resolves action identities and duplicate occurrences with explicit Fn OS targeting; bounded JSON/raw-DEFLATE/zlib/gzip decoding alone is not semantic interchange. Shared action-byte encoding and lookup tables are now migrated; full-layer baseline is normal defaultMatrix even for Fn. Embedded ConfigMacro payloads now convert offline to validated Linux events and slot bytes, including mouse buttons and motion; conflicting slot payloads are rejected and unresolved bindings are reported. CLI import now reserves macro IDs from other normal/Fn layers, allocates imported payloads, saves a complete recovery snapshot, and verifies macros before the selected matrix. GUI vendor import now previews and applies a single record using a one-use token and rejects changed macro allocation before writing. The child-profile audit confirms one child per normal Glyph profile and selected-value import; the outer array is not a Glyph batch import. Physical validation remains unfinished. Preview output is explicitly not write-ready. Offline vendor-record export embeds decoded macros and preserves representable bindings; hidden-slot changes and ambiguous raw macros are rejected. Exact factory Fn exports remain unrepresentable through the vendor full writer.

features.title: Firmware version and bootloader awareness
features.notes: Explicit Settings component read refreshes Glyph identity and queries USB/RF/MLED/OLED/flash with little-endian decoding and zero-as-unavailable semantics. Boot/non-Glyph modes are rejected. Physical versions and update/recovery remain unverified.

features.title: Firmware update and recovery
features.notes: CLI and disconnected Settings container inspection provide bounded raw-DEFLATE/ZIP parsing, image hashes and source-backed main/OLED payload chunk counts and additive checksums. Firmware update/recovery is still missing. Authentic Glyph metadata/images, image identity and component applicability remain unresolved; synthetic inspection tests do not validate flashing.

features.title: Vendor account/cloud/profile workflows applicable to Glyph
features.notes: Static Windows handlers separate account-independent local configuration/macro storage from login-gated cloud sharing and session-based community operations. Linux local libraries exist; vendor cloud sharing/community, full rendered/service applicability remains unresolved. Both platforms now have verified matching account guards for macro/config sharing; this does not establish all cloud control envelopes. No blanket exclusion is accepted.

features.title: Firmware retrieval and update-service dependencies
features.notes: Explicit read-only model-3059 metadata query and offline source-backed version comparison are available in the CLI and Settings. Metadata queries do not hold the device transaction lock. Actual lookup returned HTTP500 Record not found on 2026-09-16 Europe/Berlin. Update availability remains unknown; no authentic image, download workflow, or firmware write/recovery is validated.

features.title: Install and launch desktop application
features.notes: Built wheels support an XDG application-menu launcher with explicit install/update/status/uninstall commands. The launcher preserves its Python environment, opens a fresh loopback browser session, and keeps a terminal for shutdown. Removal preserves libraries/backups. Package upgrades remain explicit pip wheel installs. Service-backed activation reuses the fixed user unit; optional tray controls reopen the UI and quit the server. Native installer packaging, window hiding and desktop-session validation remain incomplete.

Native browser-window hiding, graphical startup preferences and suspend/resume remain incomplete.
